detail: Web research 2026-09-09 (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks, plugin build docs, agent-plugins.org 1.0.0 schema, changelog through 0.153.0, openai/codex source): hook matchers accept "Bash" as an alias for the shell tool and apply_patch for Edit/Write; nothing aliases commands for exec_command. PLUGIN_ROOT/PLUGIN_DATA (and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT/CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA) are documented only for plugin HOOK commands, not for skills or the agent's shell. Consequence for any CLI-based Twining in Codex: a skill cannot rely on `twining` resolving; the executable must come from a repo devDependency (npx resolves locally offline), a global install, a vendored bundle, or an absolute path a SessionStart hook injects into context. Also relevant: Codex spawns MCP stdio servers OUTSIDE the sandbox (codex-rs/rmcp-client stdio_server_launcher.rs, plain Command, no Seatbelt/bwrap) while shell commands run inside it (no network by default, cwd + /tmp writable, main checkout of a linked worktree NOT writable) — so the worktree->main store redirect would be blocked for a sandboxed CLI in a Codex worktree session, and the enterprise requirements.toml [mcp_servers] allowlist matches name + exact command identity.
summary: Codex plan's "Bash aliasing for exec_command" is a hook-matcher alias, not shell aliasing: no way for a Codex plugin to put a command on PATH or expose PLUGIN_ROOT to skills
